decisions.text: type bar: categories compared by value
nominal categories sorted by value, descending
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical bars
5 values against 6 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: $4.4 million, $4.2 million, $3.5 million, $1.7 million, $1.4 million (G6.16, G7.4)
every label just outside its bar's end: neither the text grey nor white reads on the bar's colour at 4.5 : 1 (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “in donations”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude

findings.message: the values are read as good or bad, with no comparison value or dividing value: a target, budget or average would say how to feel about them (G8.12, G0.19)
findings.title: comparison values where the audience lacks context: targets and budgets before averages, previous periods and peers

source.shows: the book's version without comparison values: nothing tells the reader how to feel about the numbers; the report asks for a target (R15-7, G8.12)
